headline: Today's sound headlines
lead: 30 new stories from 17 sound and audio news sources over the last 48 hours, including Sound On Sound, Production Expert, ProSoundWeb, FOH, TV Technology and 12 more. This edition is assembled automatically from the outlets' own feeds: titles and summaries are theirs, sorted into sections. Open a story for the full article.

craft.body:
Tools like VoxSplit and FFT can now get things out of a recording that used to be impossible. That makes it easy to forget that every separation is a guess at what was there. Always keep the untouched original on its own track or playlist, and print the separated result next to it, not in its place. Judge the result in the mix at the playback level and on the system it will be heard on, not soloed on headphones. Artefacts that disappear in context are fine, and ones that only show up in the mix are not.

Write down which tool, version and profile you used in the session notes or clip names. If the editor, mixer or QC flags something weeks later, you can repeat the process or undo it in minutes instead of guessing.
craft.title: Treat separation as a destructive edit
